detection_objective.description: Identify PowerShell process creations whose command line hides the code being run (encoded commands) or downloads and executes remote content in memory. Implemented by detection D001.

labels.rationale: User opens a text file from Explorer. Routine, non-PowerShell activity.
User starts the browser. Routine, non-PowerShell activity.
Service Control Manager starts a service host. Expected operating system behaviour.
Engineer opens an interactive PowerShell window with no arguments. PowerShell use alone is outside the detection objective.
Code editor starts PowerShell for its integrated terminal. Common developer workflow.
Scheduled task runs a named, on-disk reporting script. The script content is visible on disk, so this is outside the objective.
User checks network configuration from a command prompt. Non-PowerShell activity.
Edge case: the file name 'q4-encryption' contains the substring '-enc'. Tests that matching on a parameter name is not done with a naive substring search.
Word document spawns hidden PowerShell with an encoded command. The encoded text decodes to an inert Write-Output string.
Command line matches a download-and-execute-in-memory pattern. 198.51.100.23 is an RFC 5737 documentation address; the command was never run.

Fictional configuration-management agent passes a script via -EncodedCommand, which some legitimate tools do. It is in scope for the objective, so an alert is expected; it represents a known benign trigger for later false-positive analysis.
Edge case: upper-case process name and mixed-case abbreviated parameter (-eNc). Tests case-insensitive matching and parameter abbreviation.
Edge case: PowerShell 7 (pwsh.exe) rather than Windows PowerShell, with an encoded command launched from a spreadsheet application.
User opens the PowerShell ISE editor. Outside the objective.
Edge case: a hidden window on its own is common in legitimate automation. The script is a named on-disk file, so this is outside the objective.

Edge case: scenario represents a renamed copy of powershell.exe. The dataset has no PE metadata (e.g. process.pe.original_file_name), so a detection keyed on process name is expected to miss it. Kept as a deliberate known false-negative case.
